title: epoll multiplex leak and stall unwind — customer-visible streaming stalls and amplified retries
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported intermittent streaming stalls and large numbers of 5xx responses during a concentrated tenant surge. Post-incident investigation indicates a previously unseen interaction between our edge connection multiplexer, epoll wait behaviour on certain kernel versions, and long-running KV cache compaction on runtime nodes. The net effect: idle connections are not being drained promptly, frontend workers block on epoll timeouts, client libraries observe long request latencies and issue retries which amplify downstream queueing and lead to GPU request starvation and 5xx bursts. This ticket coordinates a short-term mitigation and a robust long-term fix across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private topologies.
impact_summary:
- Affected customers: 4 enterprise customers with high-concurrency streaming workloads reported client disconnects and spikes in 5xx rate for 3–12 minutes per incident.
- Observed symptoms: streaming stalls (clients waiting >10s for first token), sudden increase in backend queue lengths, and tenant-specific retry amplification.
- Business impact: at least two customers opened high-severity escalations to support; SLA blips for Hosted and Dedicated customers during windows.
- Frequency: two recurrence windows observed over past 48 hours tied to KV compaction cycles and a region-level traffic surge.
reproduction_steps:
1) Deploy a synthetic workload that opens many long-lived streaming connections (~1000 streams) against the Hosted edge in us-west1.
2) Trigger a backend KV compaction job on a subset of runtime nodes concurrently.
3) Observe epoll wait metrics on edge processes (latency histograms shift right) and socket backlog growth for affected workers.
4) Client-side: issue repeated requests with default SDK retry settings — observe amplified queuing and 5xx wave.
Notes: reproduction is timing-sensitive and more pronounced on Linux kernels 5.10–5.15 with our current epoll wrapper. Results are less visible on Dedicated isolated clusters (depends on network topology) and require on-prem kernel variants for Private deployments to fully reproduce.
interim_mitigations:
- Immediate: deploy edge-side connection drain patch to aggressively close idle streams older than 30s during high-load windows (fast roll, region-specific).
- SDK guidance: publish a temporary advisory recommending exponential-backoff increases for streaming clients and an opt-in lower retry cap for high-concurrency customers.
- Runtime throttling: enable a per-tenant in-flight request cap (soft limit) to prevent a single tenant from saturating GPU queues.
- Ops runbook: add playbook steps to detect epoll-wait tail increases and trigger automated connection-drain window instead of manual intervention.
long_term_fixes:
- Replace epoll wrapper with a non-blocking poll strategy and reduce global epoll wait granularity to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Refactor KV compaction to perform staggered compaction with backpressure hooks exposed to the serving runtime so compaction work does not stall request threads.
- Implement a token-bucket admission control at the edge that integrates with per-tenant quotas and informs the router to fast-fail non-critical requests (with structured error and retry-after header).
- Add a streaming health-check heartbeat and lightweight keepalive that is cheaper than a full poll cycle to keep connection multiplexers responsive.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (next 24–48h): region-limited rollout of aggressive idle-drain + per-tenant soft caps to us-west1; monitor 5xx rate and queue depth.
Phase 2 (week): SDK advisory + dashboard widgets for customers to opt into reduced retries; widen rollout of admission control to all Hosted regions.
Phase 3 (month): runtime refactor (epoll replacement + staggered compaction) landed, e2e QA on Dedicated clusters, then Private customer upgrade lanes with kernel compatibility notes.
Rollback plan: revert idle-drain if we observe unexpected client data loss; revert soft caps if we see excessive fast-fails and escalate for manual handling.
acceptance_criteria:
- Incidents of streaming stalls reduce to zero in canary region for three continuous 24h windows under synthetic surge.
- No customer-visible increase in completed request error rates after rollout of soft caps (customers with opt-in retain previous behaviour).
- Successful end-to-end test coverage for new admission control and compaction backpressure hooks.
- Playbook updated and support trained for detection and mitigation steps.
monitoring_and_alerts:
- New metric: edge.epoll_wait_95 (ms) per process, region and host.
- New alert: epoll_wait_95 > 200ms for >3 hosts in a region -> P1 paging.
- Dashboard: per-tenant in-flight counts, queue depth, and rapid retry rate.
- Logs: structured markers for connection_drain events and admission_control rejections.
- Post-deploy: 72h automated canary analysis comparing 5xx rate and p50/p95 latency to pre-deploy baseline.
comments: 2026-03-10 — Aisha Malik: Initial triage complete. Captured kernel traces and identified epoll wait tail. Recommended immediate idle-drain hotpatch while we investigate deeper.

2026-03-11 — Carlos Ortega: Deployed idle-drain hotpatch to canary region; observed 60% reduction in streaming stalls but an increase in client reconnects for one customer — reached out to PMs for coordinated comms.

2026-03-11 — Priya Desai (oncall): Added alerting for epoll_wait_95 and dashboard for per-tenant queue depth. Noted that Dedicated clusters show similar behaviour when compaction and heavy streaming coincide.

2026-03-12 — Design review (Liam Chen): Raised concern about aggressive idle-drain impacting long-running interactive sessions; suggested a conservative default with customer opt-out for known long-lived workflows.
2026-03-12 — Carlos Ortega: Proposal to land token-bucket admission control as next step; opened design doc and scheduled architecture sync with infra and runtime teams.
